title: "Data"

Most examples in this course use data from a real study. It evaluated the impact of Mindspark, a learning software, on children's learning in after-school centers in Delhi, India.

- [A short, non-technical summary of the study](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/disrupting-education-evidence-technology-aided-instruction-india)
- [The academic article](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20171112)
- [A 3-minute video about the study](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fpChwrfYnI8)

## Download the data

Anyone can use these files, whether you're in the class, teaching a similar one, or learning on your own. Each opens in Excel, Google Sheets or R.

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| [`ms_blel_jpal_long.csv`](../files/data/mindspark/ms_blel_jpal_long.csv) | All 1,158 rows: one per student, per round |
| [`ms_blel_jpal_baseline.csv`](../files/data/mindspark/ms_blel_jpal_baseline.csv) | The 619 students at baseline |
| [`ms_blel_jpal_endline.csv`](../files/data/mindspark/ms_blel_jpal_endline.csv) | The 539 students at endline |
| [`codebook.csv`](../files/data/mindspark/codebook.csv) | What each of the 36 variables means |
| [`README.txt`](../files/data/mindspark/README.txt) | Source, license and what we changed |

The data are deidentified: each student has a study ID, and no names.

These are the data sheets from the workbook used in EDUC 15 in Fall 2024. We saved them as CSV files and corrected two labels in the codebook. For the authors' original files, see their [replication package on openICPSR](https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/project/113192/version/V2/view).
